Department:  Public Utilities
Submitted by:  Adriana Ramos, Administrative Analyst

Subject
Presentation of the Stakeholder Survey Results

Recommendation
No action is required by the Commissions. This is a presentation only.

Background
The California Energy Commission (CEC) requires Publicly Owned Utilities to create an
Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) every five years. IRPs describe how utilities plan to meet their
energy and capacity resource needs, policy goals, physical and operational constraints, and
other utility priorities while maintaining competitive rates. Pursuant to Public Utilities Code (PUC)
Section 9621, IRPs are reviewed by the CEC to ensure they meet various law policies and
regulations, including greenhouse gas emission reduction targets and renewable energy
procurement requirements. The City of Vernon (City) filed its last IRP in 2018 and is currently
creating its new plan.

On March 21, 2023, City Council approved a services agreement with Ascend Analytics, LLC
(Ascend) to assist in the development of an IRP. Together, the City and Ascend will analyze the
City’s demand forecast and energy efficiency programs, review the City’s existing and proposed
energy resources and programs, examine the City’s interconnections and distribution facilities,
and assess renewable energy and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance.

As the IRP will provide a comprehensive strategy to deliver reliable service, maintain competitive
rates, and achieve environmental goals, the City has sought guidance and feedback from its
stakeholders. To that end, Vernon Public Utilities provided questionnaires to community
stakeholders to gauge interest in important factors that will shape the utility’s future. The purpose
of this presentation is to present the survey results.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

PUBLIC COMMENT

PRESENTATIONS

1.  Presentation on the Integrated Resource Plan Survey and Upcoming
  Outreach Efforts
  Recommendation: No action required by the Commissions. This is a presentation
  only.

  Public Utilities Integrated Resources Manager Raufdeen presented the staff
  report.

  In response to Commissioner questions, Public Utilities Integrated Resources
  Manager Raufdeen stated the previous IRP was available on the City’s website.
  He discussed means of promoting the survey and efforts to include prospective
  stakeholders; renewable requirements and resources; efforts to meet the 2045
  California mandate; and State mandates for both public-owned and investor-
  owned utilities. He acknowledged the challenge of meeting State regulations while
  prioritizing reliability and low rates. He confirmed the IRP would model renewable
  options, and thus present the least cost gap necessary to achieve these goals. He
  stated plans for converting MGS to become a green asset would also be included
  in the IRP study. Public Utilities Business and Account Supervisor Serrano
  explained that businesses utilizing solar were based on NEM (Net Metering
  program), which prevented customers from over producing energy and thus could
  not assist with meeting renewable requirements.

  In response to Commission questions, staff explained energy produced by Hoover

  rooftop solar energy; Vernon Public Utilities’ efforts to work with businesses on
  solar/battery energy; greenhouse gas technology; the City’s renewable contracts
  and future renewable contracts; and use of food waste for generation of electricity.
